title: Approved surfaces and equipment boundaries
audience: Cleaners who may be asked to clean laboratory surfaces and equipment.
learningOutcomes: Identify the approved surface inventory and treat ambiguous surfaces as excluded.
Explain why specialist equipment, such as biological safety cabinets, stays under its equipment manager.
Refuse and reassign a request to clean inside specialist equipment, and log it as out of scope.

instruction.heading: What the approved surface inventory is
instruction.body: The approved surface inventory is the laboratory's written list of the surfaces that may be cleaned as housekeeping, the method and products that apply to each, and the no-touch margins around equipment that must not be cleaned by the cleaning team. It is usually a set of plans or a table tied to room numbers, and it is maintained by the laboratory or its equipment manager. Your authority to clean a surface comes from this list and nothing else. A surface that looks like an approved surface, is next to one, or was cleaned last month is not automatically on the list. Before you start, compare the room you are in with the inventory, check the room number and the date of the inventory, and identify each surface you plan to touch. If the inventory has been changed since your last visit, ask the equipment manager for the current version before you begin.

instruction.heading: Ambiguity is an exclusion
instruction.body: Where a surface is not clearly on the inventory, treat it as excluded until the equipment manager clarifies it. Ambiguity is not permission. Common ambiguous cases include the top of a piece of equipment, a shelf above a bench, a panel that may be part of an enclosure, a splash guard, the frame around a door to a controlled room, and a tray that sits on or under equipment. Each of these may be part of a containment or airflow system even when it looks like an ordinary surface. Do not clean it, do not move it, and do not decide that the nearby approved surface covers it. Note the surface on your record, describe where it is, and ask the equipment manager to classify it in writing. The written answer then goes on the inventory or the job file, so that the next cleaner does not have to guess.

instruction.heading: Specialist equipment stays with its equipment manager
instruction.body: Biological safety cabinets, centrifuges and fume hoods are specialist equipment. They are operated, checked and maintained by people who are trained for them, and their interiors and airflow can be disturbed by unapproved cleaning. A biological safety cabinet uses controlled airflow through its front opening to protect the people and work inside it, and wiping the inside without the approved method can change that airflow or contaminate the work surface. Some interiors are cleaned only by trained laboratory personnel under a documented method, and that method may include steps that a housekeeping cleaner is not trained to carry out. A cleaner does not clean the inside of this equipment unless the equipment manager has put that task in writing, with the method and the person authorised to do it. The outside of the equipment may be in scope, but only where the inventory lists it, and the no-touch margin around the opening is excluded unless the inventory says otherwise.

instruction.heading: A request to clean inside equipment
instruction.body: Suppose a cleaner is asked to wipe the inside of a biological safety cabinet. The request may come from a senior person, a researcher, or a colleague who is trying to save time, and the source does not change the answer. The request is out of scope for the cleaner. Decline it politely and clearly, reassign it to trained laboratory personnel, and log the request as out of scope with the time, the person who asked, the reason and the name of the person it was reassigned to. Do not treat the request as a quick favour, and do not wipe the outside and report that the inside was done. If the person insists, ask them to put the request in writing from the equipment manager or the laboratory supervisor. A cleaner who cannot get that instruction in writing does not carry out the task. The log protects the cleaner, the laboratory and the equipment, because it shows what was asked and what was done.

instruction.heading: Products, SDS and the chemical register
instruction.body: Use only the cleaning products approved for the surfaces you are working on, and check the label and the safety data sheet before you use any product. The Safe Work Australia guidance says the hazardous chemicals register must cover the hazardous chemicals used, handled or stored at the workplace, that each entry needs a current safety data sheet attached, and that the register must be readily accessible to workers. A product that is not on the approved list, or that has no current safety data sheet available, is not used. Ask for the product's entry on the register before you start, and do not mix products to make a stronger solution. The products you use must match the surfaces in the inventory, because a product approved for a bench may not be approved for an instrument surface.

instruction.heading: Recording and returning
instruction.body: Make a minimal record of the zone, the surfaces classified as approved, the surfaces classified as excluded, the excluded task, the responsible contact, the time, the follow-up and the return criteria. Resume only when the site authority has given an updated scope, and only in the areas that scope names. The handover covers housekeeping only, with no sterilisation or decontamination claim. A record that says a cabinet was cleaned, or that a room is sterile, is a claim that the cleaner cannot prove, and it must not be written. State what was tidied, what was not touched, and what remains with the equipment manager. This lesson does not authorise cleaning inside biological safety cabinets, centrifuges or fume hoods, and it does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority.

procedure: Confirm the room, the date and the version of the approved surface inventory, and ask for the current version if it has changed.
Identify each surface you plan to touch on the inventory, and check the no-touch margins before starting.
Treat any ambiguous surface as excluded until the equipment manager classifies it in writing.
Use only products approved for the approved surfaces, and check the register entry and the safety data sheet for each product.
Decline and reassign any request to clean inside specialist equipment, and do not wipe the outside and report the inside as done.
Log the out-of-scope request with the time, requester, reason and the person it was reassigned to.
Complete a housekeeping-only handover, recording the classified surfaces, the exclusions and the return criteria.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner is asked to wipe the interior of a biological safety cabinet by a researcher who says the cabinet is due for a clean and that it will only take a minute.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, what do you record, and what do you tell the researcher?
workedExamples.reasoning: Decline the task and say that the interior is reassigned to trained laboratory personnel under the equipment manager's method. Do not wipe the interior or the outside and report the inside as done. Log the request as out of scope with the time, the researcher's name, the reason and the person it was reassigned to. Ask the researcher to send the request to the equipment manager. The cleaner resumes only the approved surfaces named in the inventory.

workedExamples.situation: A bench has a strip of metal along its back edge that is not clearly marked on the inventory. It looks like the bench top, but it is at the same height as the splash guard of a fume hood beside it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the strip approved for cleaning, and how do you classify it?
workedExamples.reasoning: Treat the strip as excluded because it is ambiguous. Its height and position suggest it may be part of the fume hood's enclosure, and the inventory does not confirm it. Clean the bench top only where the inventory names it, keep out of the no-touch margin, and record the strip with its position and the time. Ask the equipment manager to classify it in writing. The bench top may be cleaned, but the strip is left until it has a written classification.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds a spray bottle of general-purpose cleaner on a bench in a laboratory, with no label that matches the approved product list and no safety data sheet on file.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you use it on the approved surfaces, and what do you do with the bottle?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use the product. It is not on the approved list and no current safety data sheet is available, so the register entry cannot be checked. Record the bottle, its location and the time, and tell the laboratory supervisor. Ask for the product's entry on the hazardous chemicals register and its safety data sheet. Use only the approved product, and do not move the unlabelled bottle to a different place.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved surface inventory and no-touch margin diagram for the room, with its version date.
Out-of-scope request log, with time, requester, reason and reassigned person.
Products approved for the approved surfaces only, each with a current safety data sheet available on site.

Site-approved gloves and eye protection for the approved housekeeping products, as set by the product's safety data sheet and the site procedure. Personal protective equipment is a last resort after higher-level controls, and it does not extend the cleaner's scope into specialist equipment.
A clean cloth or cleaning tool for each approved surface, kept separate from the tools used elsewhere where the site requires it.

commonErrors.error: Wiping inside equipment because the request came from a senior person.
commonErrors.prevention: The interior is reassigned to trained personnel. Ask for the request in writing from the equipment manager.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning an ambiguous surface because it looks similar to an approved one.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat ambiguity as excluded and ask the equipment manager for a written classification.

commonErrors.error: Entering the no-touch margin to reach a corner.
commonErrors.prevention: Stay out of the margin unless the inventory allows it. Reach the corner by another approved route, or leave it.

commonErrors.error: Using a product from a cupboard without checking the register or the safety data sheet.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only approved products, and check the register entry and the safety data sheet first.

commonErrors.error: Wiping the outside of a cabinet and recording the inside as cleaned.
commonErrors.prevention: Record only what was done. The inside is not done, and the record must say so.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Safe Work Australia describes the hazardous chemicals register as covering hazardous chemicals used, handled or stored at a workplace, with a current safety data sheet for each entry, and readily accessible to workers. Check the state or territory WHS regulator for any extra rules that apply to the site.
Laboratory equipment, including biological safety cabinets, centrifuges and fume hoods, is covered by the operator's procedures. This lesson does not authorise cleaning inside any of them.

Safe Work Australia describes personal protective equipment as a last resort after higher-level controls, and places the duty to provide it and train people in its use on the person conducting the business or undertaking.
This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

qualityStandard: Approved surface inventory used to classify each surface in the desk exercise, with ambiguous surfaces recorded as excluded.
No-touch margins identified and respected in the case study.
Out-of-scope request declined, reassigned and logged with all required fields.
Only approved products used, with the register entry and safety data sheet checked before use.
No sterilisation, decontamination or clearance claim in the record or handover.
documentationEvidence: Surface classification sheet showing approved, excluded and ambiguous surfaces, with the inventory version date.
Out-of-scope request log with time, requester, reason and reassigned person.
Minimal deferral record with the responsible contact and the return criteria.
Housekeeping-only handover with the exclusions listed.
summary: Your authority to clean a surface comes only from the approved surface inventory.
Ambiguous surfaces are excluded until the equipment manager classifies them in writing.
Specialist equipment interiors stay with the equipment manager and trained personnel.
Decline and reassign out-of-scope requests, log them, and never report a clearance.

knowledgeChecks.question: You are asked to wipe inside a biological safety cabinet. What is correct?
options: Wipe it, because the request is simple and quick and the cabinet looks easy
Wipe the outside and record that the inside was done, so the job is complete
Decline, reassign to trained laboratory personnel, and log the request as out of scope

knowledgeChecks.question: A surface is not clearly on the approved inventory. What do you do?
options: Clean it because it looks like the approved surfaces next to it
Treat it as excluded until the equipment manager classifies it in writing
Skip the record and move on to the next area without any note at all

knowledgeChecks.question: What must the out-of-scope request log record?
options: Nothing, if the rest of the job is finished and the bench is clean
The time, the requester, the reason, and the person it was reassigned to
Only the cost of the cleaning product that was used on the bench

knowledgeChecks.question: You find an unlabelled cleaning bottle with no safety data sheet on file. What is correct?
options: Use it on the approved surfaces, since it is already in the room
Do not use it, record it, and ask for its register entry and safety data sheet
Mix it with the approved product to make it stronger for the bench
